target_customer: Consumers: first webcam owners wanting motion highlights, later phone users wanting auto edited movies
problem: People record far more video than they watch or edit; the product condensed footage to the moments that matter.
business_model: Freemium with ads at launch, premium at $8.99 a month for the webcam service
product_category: Video capture and automatic video editing

founders.name: Michael Katsevman
founders.background_notes: YC bio: a prehistoric YC founder.

competitors.name: Animoto
competitors.what: Automatic video montages from photos and clips, added video and iPhone app in 2009

technical_complexity.rationale: Motion detection on webcam streams then automatic highlight editing across mobile and desktop required real video processing work.

defensibility.rationale: Algorithms were copyable and rivals such as Animoto and later Magisto targeted the same job.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes incumbent action; later automatic editors such as Magisto emerged after founding.

market_need_then: Video was growing on phones and webcams; launch coverage cites Justin.tv using it for pet cams. The 2012 raise was described as supporting a mobile product.

branding.domain_note: highlightcam.com now redirects to a New Zealand site, highlightcam.co.nz, an unrelated sports app; not followed.

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the brand beyond the name and a short YC profile, so no evidence of brand pull was found.

pivots.to: Automatic mobile and desktop movie editing
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; the later product is described by YC and 2012 coverage. Exact pivot date not sourced.

outcome_analysis: HighlightCam started in 2009 as a motion highlight webcam service, then became an automatic movie editor and raised about $3 million in a Series A reported in 2011 and 2012 with Quest, Docomo Capital and Digital Garage. It is listed inactive and one database marks it dead, but no credible shutdown reason was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: The two Series A items (Fortune 2011-11, $2.8M of a $4.1M round; Global Venturing 2012-08, $3M) probably describe one round closing; CB Insights total of $3.02M over 3 rounds supports roughly $3M, so the total may not be additive. 500 Startups and YC seed amounts not found. Animoto competitor is relevant to the later editing product, the 2009 product was webcam monitoring where no competitor was named. A startup database gives a shutdown cause, rejected as unreliable. Education and employers not found.
